Hebrew text is `written using a 22-letter consonantal abjad script` and is read and written **from right to left**.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Introduction/Basic_Features/basic_features.html)

### Key Features of Hebrew Text

- **Alphabet & Vowels:** The alphabet contains 22 basic letters with **no lowercase or capital letters** . Vowels are traditionally omitted in standard writing, though dots and dashes called *niqqud* are added in children's books, poetry, and religious texts to show vowel sounds.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wQLwNbeuAJM)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Introduction/Basic_Features/basic_features.html)
- **Final Letters:** Five letters (*kaf, mem, nun, peh, tzade* ) change their shape when they appear at the very end of a word (called *sofit*).[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ekc3lIVdHEU)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Introduction/Basic_Features/basic_features.html)
- **Script Evolution:** Modern Hebrew uses the square block script (derived from Aramaic-style script), while ancient texts were written in Paleo-Hebrew. Everyday handwriting uses a distinct cursive script.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleo-Hebrew_alphabet)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Unit_One/Pictograms/pictograms.html)
- **Online Tools:** You can practice typing or generate script using digital options like the [Hebrew Keyboard Online - Lexilogos](https://www.lexilogos.com/keyboard/hebrew.htm) or the [Hebrew Keyboard (מקלדת עברית)](https://gate2home.com/Hebrew-Keyboard).[[1]](https://www.lexilogos.com/keyboard/hebrew.htm)[[2]](https://gate2home.com/Hebrew-Keyboard)

If you have a specific word or phrase, tell me:

- Would you like it **transliterated** (written in Latin letters)?
- Do you need a **translation** into English?
- Are you looking for **vowel marks (*niqqud*)** included?
